Subject: Clarify metering boundaries: system vs tool tokens and rounding rules

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. As you review the draft rate card we sent, you had a couple of very specific metering questions that I promised to follow up on: how we attribute system messages vs. tool (function) tokens, and where rounding occurs (per-call vs. per-invoice). Below is our current understanding plus a few concrete examples attached (metering-examples.xlsx). Can you confirm these are the scenarios you care about, or add any others?

Summary of the current policy (high level):
- Input tokens: prompt tokens sent to the model, including explicit system messages and user messages, are billed at the input rate.
- Output tokens: tokens generated by the model (including text returned when the model calls a function and that result is returned to the chat) are billed at the output rate.
- Tool-only work: if you call an external tool/service from your app (e.g., run a DB query / semantic search) and the result is not produced by the model itself (i.e., you fetch data outside the model and send it to the user without model generation), Redwood does not bill those bytes as model tokens.

Open nuance items I flagged for internal confirmation:
1) Function-call payloads: when the model triggers a function_call, if the function response is marshalled back into the model as part of a subsequent prompt (and thus tokenized), those tokens count as input tokens on that follow-up call. If the model returns the function response directly to the user as generated text, those tokens are output tokens.
2) System message tokens: system messages included in the prompt are billed as input; this includes programmatic system prompts we add for safety/formatting.
3) Streaming and rounding: streaming responses are billed on the final token counts for the call. We round at the token level (integer tokens — there are no fractional tokens). The practical question you raised was whether we round per-stream-chunk or only on call completion — answer: we compute exact token boundaries via the tokenizer and bill on the completed call (so partial chunks are not separately rounded up).

I attached a small workbook with examples (prompt with 42.3k characters, how that tokenizes, tool call sequences, and expected per-call billing). Also attached the redlined rate card PDF.

If that mapping matches what you're reviewing, Marcus and I can draft a short billing appendix for the SOW that spells this out and includes a few canonical examples for audits.

Next steps: can you confirm the three scenarios above (function_call being input vs output depending on flow, system messages billed as prompt, rounding applied at call completion) are the behaviors you need called out for procurement?

Thanks for the quick summary and the attachments. A few clarifying points from our side so we can sign off internally:

Emily —

Thanks for the concrete asks. Quick answers while I pull in Finance for the discount math.

1) Tool / search payloads: If your app fetches documents from your index and sends them into the model prompt (even as a structured field), those tokens are billed as input tokens on that model call — because the model tokenizes what it receives. If instead your app calls the search and renders results to users without sending those bytes into the model, there is no model token charge. So the key is whether the model is tokenizing the content.

Example: flow A (model triggers search, app returns raw search results, app formats locally) — only the tokens sent into the model are billed. Flow B (model receives search results as part of the prompt) — those tokens are billed as input.

2) Streaming / reconnects: we bill based on finalized model calls. Our runtime will credit accidental duplicated partials (retries due to network) as long as they're within the same call-id and happen within the standard retry window; we can include language in the SOW about credits for retry storms. The streaming chunks are not individually rounded — the tokenizer boundaries are deterministic and billing is on final token counts for the call.

I'll loop in Finance for the discount/rounding ordering; Grace, can you confirm the standard invoicing flow?

—Marcus

Hi all —

Couple notes from Finance and Contracts:

- Rounding and discount ordering: we compute exact integer token totals per-call (there are no fractional tokens). For invoicing, we sum the integer token counts across the billing period, apply the agreed tiered discounts to the aggregated token totals, compute the dollar amount, and then round the final invoice to the nearest cent. In short: discount is applied to the aggregated token-based charge before currency rounding.

- Discounts / tiers: for your committed-usage agreement (ACME-2027-S1) we apply a volume discount at the invoice-level, not per-call. That means you get the volume band pricing applied to the total token buckets for the month.

- Credits for retries: we already have an automated de-dupe that looks for transient retry storms and credits obviously duplicated calls within a short reconciliation window. We'll add explicit language to the SOW appendix that any retry-related overages that meet the 'retry storm' criteria will be credited upon reconciliation.

- Examples: see meter-examples tab in the spreadsheet. One important thing to call out: tokens generated by model->function_call->model cycles can cross the input/output boundary depending on where we serialize the function result. We recommend an SOW appendix that defines canonical flows (A: tool-as-input, B: tool-as-output) with per-flow examples so both billing and audit teams can reconcile token lines to application logs.

Marissa — FYI (she's the owner for any contract language tweaks).
